properties.name: COUNTED across one session: twelve places where a record still read confident after the thing it described had moved — and the tools caught seven of them unprompted
properties.statement:
SYNTHESIS OF ONE SESSION, 2026-08-21, eight merged PRs (#281–#288). Recorded because the pattern exists in no single node — each instance is written on its own node and none of them says there were twelve.

THE SHAPE: a record goes on asserting something after the thing it describes has moved, and nothing about the record looks wrong. It is not a wrong record; it is a record that has stopped being checked against anything.

=== THE INSTANCES, all found or fixed this session ===

  1. `rel:v0380` carried `status: planned` while tagged, published, deployed and asset-verified.
  2. `release_without_epoch` exempted any `planned` release — so it would have excused exactly the release above. A status field trusted where an edge was the truth.
  3. `dec:one-process-many-stores` — `status: accepted`, name "ACCEPTED 2026-08-06", body opening "PROPOSED, NOT SETTLED."
  4. `dec:core-api-spof-accepted` named a topology BL-83a had moved; the judgement was right and the sentence was stale.
  5. `ifc:core-api` was `published` — in the document handed to a vendor — for a crate nobody outside can link.
  6. `ifc:core-api`'s `spec` field held a 2026-07-28 changelog note where the specification belongs.
  7. `ifc:core-api`'s `payload_schema` read `unspecified` while ELEVEN artifacts carried SPECIFIES edges at it.
  8. `ifc:kv-backend` (dynograph-foundation) is `published` in the design and `pub(crate)` in the code.
  9. `unverified_capability` asked 28 unbuilt roadmap rows to prove themselves — a list that could not reach zero.
 10. `open_questions`, the first call of every session and documented as cheap, costs 11.7s of which 10.3 is a defect sweep nobody asked for; and "the first store read costs 26–48s" had been carried for weeks as the STORE being slow, which it is not.
 11. `seam_report` returned `incompatible: 0` beside `unstated: 30`, and the August PoC's `unmet_needs: 0` beside `dead_surface: 15` — zeros that read as health and mean nobody said anything.
 12. An analysis was RE-DERIVED that `dec:linked-repos-poc` had already done, better, on 2026-08-06.

⭐ THE FIX WAS THE SAME SHAPE EVERY TIME, AND IT WAS NEVER MORE PROSE. Each one closed by making the disagreement VISIBLE somewhere that fails: a detector keyed on an edge rather than a status; a gate that turns red; a count asserted in a test; a field that says "this cannot be enumerated" instead of sitting blank; a note recording that somebody looked and found nothing. A promise written in a decision is not a guard — that recurred three times on its own (the release procedure, the SPOF description, and the local-case protection flo2's work would test).

⭐⭐ AND THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE MATTERS MORE THAN THE COUNT. SEVEN of the twelve were caught by the design's own machinery, unprompted, while doing something else:
  — the dedup guard refused four near-duplicate writes and named what to read;
  — `create_node`'s revision note said "no snapshot holds the state it replaced — checked, not assumed", which is the only reason a Decision's prior wording survives;
  — compare-and-swap refused a stale hash;
  — the export divergence guard refused to drop a claim edge and named it;
  — `reflow2_check` refused a severed lineage chain mid-fold;
  — `loop_status` reported its OWN server as stale, which is why the performance numbers were re-measured rather than trusted;
  — `seam_report` refused to call 30 unstated axes agreement.
So the pattern is not that the design rots unnoticed. It is that the design notices exactly where somebody built a place for it to notice, and nowhere else.

⚠️ LIMITS. "Twelve" is a count of what one session happened to touch, not a survey — nobody swept the design for this shape, and a sweep would find more. Instances 1–9 are verifiable on their nodes; 10 and 11 are on their own TemporalFacts; 12 is recorded on `fact:the-seam-report-half-of-the-poc-finally-ran`. The claim that the fix was "the same shape every time" is a reading of twelve cases by the agent that worked them, and is the softest thing here.
